g.text: HR-1 TAKES THESE OUT
Provider tax limits
federal match never drawn
Home equity cap −$0.0026
will not pass the home equity test for long-term care
Immigrant eligibility ended −$0.06
will not be eligible — but see the injunction below
Retroactive coverage ended −$0.04
will not be covered for the months before the claim
Work reporting −$2.86
will not enroll; would have reached disbursements
Six-month renewals −$0.46
will not survive renewal; would have reached the payer
Renewal automation blocked −$0.29
will not be renewed without a form the District already has
Reconsideration period blocked −$0.14
will not come back after a paperwork lapse
Medicare Savings rule suspended −$1.74
2023 rule; dual eligibles pay these Medicare costs themselves
Directed payment caps
will not top up hospital, nursing facility, academic rates
NOT SHOWN, AND NOT ESTIMATED
• MODELLED. DC's FY2024 hundred grown to FY2030 at the prior-law rate implied by the national
model's own counterfactual — basis_national's FY2024 hundred against tobe2030's FY2030 prior-law
total, CBO January 2025 baseline vintage. Derived in code, never typed. Corroborated by, not derived
from, DC's own observed growth of 5.49% on Exhibit 16 FY2022-24. SUPERSESSION HUNTED AND NOT FOUND,
2026-10-29: both DHCF agency chapters, the FY2026 budget testimony, the FY2026 budget slides and the
June 2025 MCAC budget presentation all stop at the budget year, and the District publishes its
four-year plan at District and fund level rather than as an agency Medicaid trajectory. Not proved
absent — the Executive Summary volume of the FY2026 Proposed budget is unchecked. The
national-implied rate stands until then.
• Public-company earnings and dual-plan retention: no DC figure
• The payer lanes are the FY2024 composition rescaled proportionally onto the FY2030 disbursement,
which the HR-1 levers have already reduced. Proportional because the stated assumption is that the
shape of the dollar does not move, only its level; no lane is claimed to absorb more of a lever than
another. A lever that falls on one lane in particular would break that, and would be drawn
differently.
• Ten of the ten HR-1 tributaries are derived on District inputs. Where a lane is derived, nothing
is allocated from CBO's national score: the denominators are DHCF's, the dollars are DHCF's, and
where a rate is modelled it is declared as one. Each lane that is not derived records what would be
needed to derive it from District sources.
• The seniors lane is derived on a District denominator and is an UPPER BOUND. The District's own
QMB-only enrolment, as a share of the national QMB-only count, applied to CBO's score for the lever;
both counts are published and both were checked to be the same definition before they were divided.
The District runs the QMB group ONLY, to 300% of the poverty line against a federal floor of 100%,
so it has already enrolled much of the population a blocked federal streamlining rule would have
reached. The band therefore runs from the figure drawn DOWN to zero rather than around it. The
District's per-$100 exposure comes out above the national one because it is over-represented in this
group relative to its Medicaid spending — a finding, not a fault. Closing the band needs one count
DHCF holds and does not publish: how many of those enrollees sit above the federal floor.
• There is no residual lane on this panel. Nationally “Everything else” is a remainder defined by
what CBO scored, which cannot be re-derived from District sources because it is not a thing. It was
retired here and three named District provisions were written in its place — the LTSS home equity
cap, the legal immigrant eligibility restriction, and retroactive coverage — each struck on CBO’s
published FY2030 section figure and a District share. All three are now sized; the declaration that
none was sized was true until section figures replaced ten-year totals and is withdrawn. Nothing on
this panel is comparable lane-to-lane with the national residual. The immigrant provision is under a
preliminary injunction and its status is contested.
• The two enrolment levers rest on one modelled step: the share of the expansion group that does not
survive them. It is published as a band with a declared default inside it, and the default is the
rate implied by CBO's own score rather than a figure of our choosing. THE BAND'S ENDS ARE NOT
LIKE-FOR-LIKE WITH ITS DEFAULT: the default is a share of expansion-group spending, which includes
people the requirement exempts, while the Arkansas and New Hampshire outcomes are coverage loss
among those subject to the requirement. Until the District's exempt share is established the upper
end is an upper bound.
• Provider tax limits and directed payment caps are coupled in the District and are not coupled in
the national model. DC's directed payments are financed by a hospital provider tax, the tax freeze
returns the programme to its FY2025 level in FY2027, and the phase-down then runs on that reverted
base from FY2029. The coupling is now MODELLED IN SEQUENCE. The two lanes do not double-count
because they are not the same dollar: the tax lever is non-federal FINANCING that will not be
collected and leaves at state government, the directed payment lever is a PAYMENT that will not be
made and leaves at claims. Two stages of one event, drawn where the money actually stops.
• The provider tax lever is published at the NON-FEDERAL level. In the District the dedicated tax is
the non-federal share and it draws federal match, so a dollar of tax never collected costs more than
a dollar of Medicaid. The multiplier is not established and is declared absent rather than guessed.
This is a divergence from the national treatment, not an application of it.
• Section 71115's rate taper does not reach the District at all. The expansion-state safe harbour
steps down to 3.5 percent by FY2032 and DC's hospital tax is 3 percent of net patient revenue, below
every step including the floor. The District's entire exposure is the freeze on taxes not imposed as
of 4 July 2025. A jurisdiction can be fully exposed to the section while sitting under every
threshold in its schedule.
• The first year of the directed payment phase-down is FY2029, resolved on the rule. CMS-2449-P
states that the phase-down begins with the first rating period starting on or after 1 January 2028,
and DC's rating period is the federal fiscal year, confirmed on two documents. A period beginning 1
October 2027 starts too early. DHCF's own budget materials say FY2028, which would make FY2030 the
third step and the reduction $145.56M; the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged, and the
model does not move to meet it.
• The phase-down does not terminate by FY2030. KFF's analysis of the approved preprints puts 100
percent of the District's hospital directed payment above the new limit, because the base rate alone
already exceeds the Medicare-based ceiling, so the programme runs down over ten steps and FY2030 at
two is partial. Stating the termination YEAR on District evidence rather than on KFF's conversion
needs DC hospitals' commercial price as a percentage of Medicare, which is not yet acquired.
• No DC service allocation is published and none has been estimated, so the claims fan is
unallocated, as in FY2024.
• The prior-law FY2030 flow holds the FY2024 composition and grows only the level. Every trunk and
lane figure on this panel is that assumption, not a projection: no DC source projects them. It
ignores known shape changes — enrolment growth concentrated among people aged 65+, dual-eligible
capitation rising faster than the rest of the book, and the District's own FY2026 eligibility
reductions.
Absent data is left absent. Filling a gap with a share would produce a modelled figure wearing a measured
figure's clothes.
